title: Bond yields hit highest since 2023 as stocks fall, oil tops $100 and buyback misfires
body: The simultaneous rise in yields, oil and equity losses (again...) points to a market pricing in sticky inflation rather than a temporary shock. Higher energy costs feed directly into headline inflation, which in turn keeps pressure on the Federal Reserve to consider further tightening even as growth risks build. The failure of the tripled Treasury buyback to bring yields down is arguably the more telling signal, since it suggests investors are demanding compensation for fiscal and supply concerns that a liquidity operation cannot fix. With the Fed's meeting a week away, traders are likely to stay defensive into the data, and any further upside surprise on inflation could extend the equity slide and keep yields elevated. --- Markets are flashing a rare combination of rising yields, rising oil and falling stocks all at once, and Wednesday's failed buyback intervention suggests policymakers are running low on quick fixes.

title: US Crude Inventories Fall in Early September
body: US crude oil inventories declined by 300,000 barrels in the week ended September 4, following a 2.6 million-barrel draw the previous week. Over the past 21 weeks, commercial crude stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) have fallen by just over 48 million barrels, although overall US crude inventories remain 2.8 million barrels higher year to date. To support commercial supply, an additional 1.2 million barrels were released from the SPR, reducing total SPR holdings to 285.4 million barrels. This level is close to the generally accepted operational minimum of 250–300 million barrels. At Cushing, Oklahoma, inventories fell by 300,000 barrels, partially reversing a 200,000-barrel increase the week before. US crude production in the week ended August 28 edged up to 13.862 million barrels per day from 13.843 million barrels per day. In refined products, gasoline inventories declined by 1.9 million barrels, while distillate inventories increased by 2 million barrels. title: Crude Oil Hits Highest Since May on US-Iran War
body: Crude oil climbed to about $96.70 a barrel on Wednesday—its highest level since May—driven by escalating tensions between the United States and Iran. US officials said Iran attempted to attack Navy vessels on Monday, following a weekend barrage in which Iranian forces targeted an aircraft carrier with ballistic missiles in a previously undisclosed wave of assaults. Iranian state media, meanwhile, reported that a US missile struck a small oil tanker roughly four miles off Kharg Island on Tuesday. The conflict widened this week after Iran-backed Houthi militants launched strikes on several energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, prompting a temporary shutdown of some operations. These developments followed US military action on Saturday, when American forces hit three Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for Iran's ballistic missile attacks on two US Navy warships. Price pressures were further amplified by a decline in US crude inventories, which fell by 0.3 million barrels last week. In addition, Ukrainian drones struck infrastructure in Novorossiysk—Russia's key Black Sea oil terminal—on Wednesday, adding another layer of risk to global supply. title: Ibovespa Slips on Political Risks and Inflation Fears
body: The Ibovespa slipped 0.9% on Wednesday, closing at 185,629 points, pressured by a resurgence of political risk in Brazil and escalating tensions in the Middle East. Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the reinstatement of Federal Police chief Andrei Rodrigues, granting an emergency petition just one day after Justice André Mendonça had determined his removal. Mendonça, who is leading a wide-ranging fraud probe involving failed lender Banco Master, had accused the Federal Police of illegally surveilling him and other public officials. The episode underscores Brazil's deepening political polarization in the run-up to the October presidential election. At the same time, intensifying conflict in the Middle East drove oil prices higher, reigniting inflation concerns. Major banks retreated, with Itaú shedding 2% and Bradesco falling 2.4%. Utilities also ended in negative territory, including Axia, which dropped 1.9%. WEG (-1.8%) and Ambev (-1.5%) further weighed on the benchmark. Bucking the broader trend, Petrobras advanced 0.7% on the back of firmer oil prices. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US API Crude Stocks Show Modest Drawdown, Easing from Prior Week's Sharp Decline
body: US crude inventories declined modestly in the latest week, with the American Petroleum Institute's Weekly Crude Oil Stock indicator coming in at -0.300 million barrels, according to data updated on 9 September 2026. The figure signals a small draw in stockpiles and marks a notable easing from the previous reading of -2.600 million barrels. The shift from a sizeable drawdown to a relatively minor inventory decrease may suggest a more balanced interplay between US oil supply and demand compared with the prior week. While stocks are still edging lower, the much smaller decline could temper expectations of tightening conditions in the crude market and may influence short-term price dynamics as traders reassess the strength of underlying demand and refinery activity.
